text:
Garry Kasparov, born Garik Weinstein in Baku, Azerbaijan, is a legendary chess player and former world champion renowned for his dynamic playing style, aggressive tactics, and deep opening preparation. A child prodigy, he became the youngest-ever world champion in 1985 at age 22, defeating Anatoly Karpov in a controversial match that was terminated without a result by FIDE. Kasparov held the world number one rating for an unprecedented 21 years (1985–2005), reaching a peak rating of 2851 in 1999. His rivalry with Karpov, known as the "two Ks," remains one of the most significant in chess history. Kasparov is also noted for his contributions to opening theory, including the "Kasparov Gambit," and his early interactions with computer chess, which culminated in his famous match against IBM's Deep Blue in 1997.
After retiring from competitive chess in 2005, Kasparov transitioned into politics, becoming a prominent opposition figure in Russia. He founded the United Civil Front and ran for president in 2008, leading to his arrest and imprisonment. He eventually fled Russia in 2013 due to persecution, citing the rise of authoritarianism under Vladimir Putin. From exile, he has vigorously criticized the Kremlin, advocating for democracy and human rights, and opposed Russia's annexation of Crimea and its invasion of Ukraine. Kasparov has also engaged in other fields, including publishing a series of biographies titled *My Great Predecessors* , writing books on decision-making and business, and advocating for Ukrainian admission to NATO. His legacy extends beyond chess to his status as a vocal dissident and a global icon of intellectual resilience.
